To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the following dietary factors inhibit colon cancer cell growth: 1) soy protein, 2) soy isoflavones, 3) green tea, 4) green tea catechins, 5) soy isoflavanoids, and 6) resveratrol.
the IGF system is a potential target in the prevention and therapy of colon cancer.
dietary phytochemicals and nutrients regulate the IGF-I system in colon cancer cells, which in turn modulates cell growth.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of dietary phytochemicals in the regulation of cell growth and the IGF system.

the effects of dietary components (e.g., soy isoflavones, green tea polyphenols, and curcumin) and their metabolites on the IGF system in the colon and their potential effects on colon cancer prevention and therapy.
understanding how the IGF system is regulated by diet and nutrition and the potential role of the IGF-I axis in the pathogenesis of colon cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the dietary components that are known to inhibit the growth of cancer cells, and that inhibit the expression and/or activity of the IGF-1 system, may be appropriate targets to reduce colon cancer risk.
a high intake of fruits, vegetables, and fiber, and moderate exercise may be beneficial in reducing the risk of colon cancer.
dietary components, especially phytochemicals, are effective modulators of the IGF-1 system and may be appropriate targets in colon cancer prevention and therapy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
dietary components, such as soybean and tea extracts, and the phytoestrogen genistein, inhibit colon cancer cell growth through modulation of the IGF-1R/PI3K/Akt pathway.

the dietary components, such as genistein, soy isoflavones, tea polyphenols, and resveratrol, inhibit the IGF-1-induced proliferation of colon cancer cells, in part, by down-regulating IGF-1 receptor expression, and by modulating the activity of the phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase/Akt signaling pathway.
the dietary components that inhibit colon cancer cell growth are those that are rich in fiber, antioxidants, and phytoestrogens.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the components of IGF system play important role in colon carcinogenesis and dietary components can modulate the expression of IGF system and its downstream signaling.
the IGF system is involved in colon cancer cell proliferation and that the components of diet and nutrition affect the IGF system.
dietary components can modulate colon cancer cell growth through the IGF system, and this effect may be due to the ability of dietary components to regulate the expression and production IGF-1.
